createdBy: codex reviewer (session 019fcbdc, T-011 plan rounds 3-6), isolated and filed by claude
impact:
This is a CROSS-TICKET contradiction, not a defect in any one plan. It was isolated over six rounds of T-011 plan review (codex session 019fcbdc), during which four separate designs to satisfy it were built and disproven.

THE CONTRACT. T-010 shipped sourceVersion as Record<string, number> documented as "Per-source offsets", and publishSnapshot admits a candidate only on STRICT DOMINANCE: every key present on both sides and at least one strictly greater (src/snapshot/dominance.ts:161-190, src/snapshot/store.ts:2180-2190). A missing key on either side is incomparable and fails closed. So every publish after the first must present per-source offsets that honestly exceed the live ones.

WHY NO v0.2 TICKET CAN PRODUCE ONE. ccusage is a black box: it consumes transcripts and emits aggregate output, and it does not report which bytes of which files it read. aggregate.ts operates on that OUTPUT. Four designs were tried and each failed on the same substitution - proving bytes were AVAILABLE and using it as proof they were CONSUMED:
  1. Read sizes before the run - can omit bytes ccusage later reads.
  2. Sample (path, size) before and after - proves size stability, used as content stability; a truncate-and-rewrite to the same length passes.
  3. Add mtime and inode - still cannot prove the state held THROUGHOUT the run, and inode revalidation is separately prohibited by T-008.
  4. Copy sources into an immutable capture - fixes destination stability only; ccusage ignoring a trailing record still publishes a stale payload under a strictly greater offset, and a truncate during the copy yields hybrid bytes of length N that were never that source's first N bytes.

T-011's plan therefore reduced to publishing ONE bootstrap generation with an empty sourceVersion (an explicit no-claim), which T-010's own rules make safe: dominance is skipped when no live manifest exists, so the first publish succeeds, and {} can never dominate anything afterwards.

WHY THE HANDOFF DOES NOT RESCUE IT. The plan then claimed T-012 would supply truthful consumed offsets for repeated refreshes. The reviewer checked T-012's own filing: T-012 ALSO uses ccusage and explicitly defers owned parsing to v0.5. Its shadows and watermarks prove what was supplied, not what was consumed. So T-012 is structurally no more able to produce this value than T-011 is. Implementing the handoff literally either leaves repeated refresh impossible or publishes fabricated dominance claims - and a fabricated sourceVersion is worse than none, because it turns the dominance rule into a mechanism for overwriting good data with stale data.

THE ACTUAL DECISION, which belongs to the owner because it changes a shipped contract:
(a) REDEFINE sourceVersion as a verified immutable-input WATERMARK rather than a consumed-offset claim, and update T-010's contracts, comments and tests to match. Dominance then means "strictly more input was made available", which is honest and is achievable in v0.2.
(b) REQUIRE A CONSUMPTION RECEIPT - owned parsing, or a ccusage change that reports consumed offsets. This is the v0.5 work, so under (b) repeated authoritative refresh does not exist in v0.2.
(c) Accept one-shot indexing for v0.2 explicitly, with repeated refresh arriving alongside owned parsing.

Until this is settled, no ticket should claim that repeated authoritative refresh works. T-011's plan has been narrowed accordingly: it publishes one bootstrap generation marked provenance.refreshTier = "bootstrap", which satisfies AC 1 with a real production-path generation, and it makes no claim about what completes it.

RELATED FIELD, same root cause: Provenance.ccusageFetchedAt is required to be a non-empty explicit instant, but ccusage 20.0.19 embeds pricing data at build time and reports no pricing-fetch timestamp. The daemon's invocation time proves only when ccusage ran, so populating it that way is the same substitution one field over - and because the field is a required scalar, the "record absence rather than a placeholder" escape that Provenance.fieldCoverage offers is not available here. Resolving (a)/(b)/(c) should settle this field's representation too, most likely as a discriminated value such as {kind:"embedded", ccusageVersion, pricingRevision} or {kind:"unknown"}.
resolution:
Resolved 2026-08-05: the owner decision this issue poses WAS MADE, recorded as N-009 (.story/notes/N-009.json) and docs/snapshot-facts-and-watermarks.md v2. The chosen option is (a) — sourceVersion is REDEFINED as a verified-input WATERMARK, with T-010's contracts, comments and tests to be updated to match — refined by codex review session 019fcfc4 into a two-part contract that option (a) alone could not honestly carry: watermarks attest RECENCY ONLY ('a maximum instant attests RECENCY, never COMPLETENESS', doc §2), and COVERAGE is attested SEPARATELY per surface on every publish via stable row identities, with disappearance allowed only trailing-edge or age-consistent-empty and anything else a typed coverage-regression refusal retaining the live generation (§3). sourceVersion's keys are SIX ingestion surfaces fixed per SCHEMA_VERSION through an executable registry (§1). Publish outcomes: published / refreshed / unchanged / refused. The consumed-offset ideal this issue proved unproducible in v0.2 'stays EXPLICITLY deferred to the v0.5 owned-parsing ticket' (T-025 item 4). So of the three options posed: (a) is adopted in strengthened form; (b)'s consumption receipt remains the v0.5 ideal; (c)'s one-shot reduction survives only as T-011's bootstrap narrowing, no longer as v0.2's ceiling.

IMPLEMENTATION IS PENDING AND OWNED, all of it inside T-025's recorded scope (.story/tickets/T-025.json, status open, parked on ISS-090/ISS-091): item 3 (the registry, the watermark/coverage publish contract, the four outcomes), item 4 ('sourceVersion semantics rewrite … contracts, comments and tests move from consumed-offset language to the RECENCY/COVERAGE SPLIT'), item 1 (registry exact-set + SnapshotPayloadV1 invariant checks). Items 2 and 5 already landed via T-026 (commit 9524902). Verified against the current tree so the closure does not overstate: src/snapshot/dominance.ts:2-4 still reads 'Dominance over per-source offset manifests … `sourceVersion` is a MANIFEST of per-source offsets'; src/snapshot/types.ts:309 and :319 still say 'Per-source offsets. Never a scalar'; publishSnapshot still requires strict dominance behind `if (live !== null)` (src/snapshot/store.ts:2180-2192). No shipping comment says 'consumed' (grep of dominance.ts/store.ts/types.ts is clean) — the surviving OFFSET vocabulary is exactly what T-025 item 4 rewrites, and until T-025 lands no ticket claims repeated authoritative refresh works: T-011's AC 10 asserts the refresh MECHANISM only and assigns the publish verdict to T-025's contract, and the T-011 plan's §12 item 5 (rewritten 2026-08-05, docs/t011-headless-service-plan.md:1298) records that ISS-075 now NARROWS T-011 to one bootstrap publish (empty sourceVersion = explicit no-claim, honest under the store's absence-is-no-claim rule) rather than blocking it. This issue's four disproven designs stay disproven; nothing in N-009 revives them.

THE RELATED-FIELD RESIDUAL (the ccusageFetchedAt paragraph above — also the residual ISS-077's resolution deferred here) is RESOLVED IN THE TREE, not lost: T-026 (commit 9524902) renamed the field to ccusageInvokedAt, meaning the instant the writer INVOKED ccusage, provable from its own clock (src/snapshot/types.ts:294-301 with the rationale comment; enforced at store.ts:960, :1077, :1084). The discriminated {kind:'embedded'|'unknown'} value this paragraph proposed was consciously NOT adopted — no required field asks for pricing recency any more, which is honest by omission rather than by placeholder (ISS-077's resolution, verified). Nothing of that residual remains open.

Closed with verification attached rather than silently, per the same rule that closed ISS-084 and ISS-077: a critical issue left open over a recorded decision is the bookkeeping lag a later session re-reads as a live blocker. The recorded reasoning — the six-round isolation, the four disproven designs — stays; it is what produced N-009.

title: No v0.2 ticket can produce a truthful sourceVersion: T-010's dominance contract requires consumed offsets that ccusage does not report
